reply:
You're absolutely right, thank you for the correction! I misspoke. Here's the accurate breakdown:

- `git stash` - only stashes tracked changes (modifications to already-tracked files)
- `git stash -u` or `git stash --include-untracked` - also includes untracked files (like your new file)
- `git stash -a` or `git stash --all` - includes both untracked and ignored files

So in your case, since your new file was untracked, plain `git stash` left it in the working tree. You would have needed `git stash -u` to stash it along with your tracked changes. Good catch!
